headerBody: Thailand: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented against Royal Thai and Tourist Police (1155) bulletins, Office of the Consumer Protection Board notices, Tourism Authority of Thailand advisories, r/Thailand reports and verified reporting from Bangkok Post and The Thaiger. Not a recycled blog list, and re-researched every year.
quadHead: Four ways Thailand catches tourists off guard.

quad.title: The Patong Jet-Ski Damage Trap
quad.tl: Operators rent visually-scratched skis, 'find' the same scratches on return, and a complicit 'officer' arrives to back a ฿30,000–฿300,000 demand.

quad.title: The Grand Palace 'Closed' Tuk-Tuk Tour
quad.tl: A friendly 'palace officer' says the Grand Palace is closed, then a 20-baht tuk-tuk ends at a gem shop with a ฿63,000 sapphire ring and two polyester suits.

quad.title: The Patpong Ping-Pong Drink Bill
quad.tl: A laminated menu promises '฿100 beers, show included'; once you sit, the real menu charges ฿700 a beer plus ฿2,000 'lady drinks' and the bill hits ฿8,000–฿87,000.

quad.title: The Night Bazaar Tailor Switch
quad.tl: A street tout steers you to a '฿2,500 custom suit' that arrives day three with polyester lining and plastic buttons — after the delivery date slips past your flight.

body: Thailand: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented against Royal Thai and Tourist Police (1155) bulletins, Office of the Consumer Protection Board notices, Tourism Authority of Thailand advisories, r/Thailand reports and verified reporting from Bangkok Post and The Thaiger — not a recycled blog list.

67 specific scams across Bangkok, Phuket, Chiang Mai, Pattaya and seven more cities. The exact scripts, the red flags that give them away, and the Thai phrases that shut them down — with a romanized exit-phrase card and Thai script you can show on your phone.

Scams evolve, so the book is re-researched and updated every year — when a new edition ships, it appears in your Kindle library. Built for the traveler who wants to move through Thailand relaxed, not braced.
